mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes SLK 55 AMG engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M113 engine for the R171 SLK 55 AMG costs £5,500-£8,500 supply-only; a rebuilt M152 engine for the R172 SLK 55 AMG costs £6,500-£10,000 supply-only. Fitting adds £1,500-£2,500 depending on complexity - AMG V8 work requires specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of crank sensor failure on a Mercedes SLK 55 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common sign is hot-start failure - the car starts fine from cold but won't restart when hot. This is a well-documented issue on the M113 engine, typically occurring around 90,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes SLK 55 AMG V8 engine (M113/M152) reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M113 is widely regarded as one of the most reliable Mercedes engines ever produced - 'almost legendary in its reliability'. The M152 is a two-generation leap forward, considered 'mega reliable' with no systemic weak points. Both engines are fundamentally strong when properly maintained.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes SLK 55 AMG engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained M113 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work. One owner reported an M113 engine still running strong at 116,500 miles. The M152 is too new for definitive long-term data but is proving reliable.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes SLK 55 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the SLK is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt M113 costs £5,500-£8,500 - far less than replacing a £10,000-£30,000 vehicle. AMG values remain strong, making engine replacement a justifiable investment for well-maintained examples.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes SLK 55 AMG V8 need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies MB 229.5 high-performance oil - typically 5W-30 or 5W-40 fully synthetic. The M113 V8 requires approximately 8.5 litres; the M152 V8 requires approximately 9.5 litres.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz SLK 55 AMG - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The SLK 55 AMG represents the pinnacle of Mercedes' compact roadster line - the only V8-powered SLK ever produced. The R171 SLK 55 AMG launched in 2004 with the M113 5.4-litre naturally aspirated V8, producing 360hp and 510Nm of torque [8†L6-L7]. This hand-built engine from Affalterbach defined the AMG brand before the turbocharging era [8†L6-L7]. In 2012, the R172 SLK 55 AMG introduced the M152 5.5-litre naturally aspirated V8, delivering 422hp and 540Nm [3†L8][3†L15-L18]. Both engines represent the last of the naturally aspirated AMG V8s in the SLK lineage.

milestones.description: M113.981, 5.4L naturally aspirated V8, 360hp @ 5,750rpm, 510Nm torque (SLK 55 AMG, R171 launch)
M152.980, 5.5L naturally aspirated V8, 422hp @ 6,800rpm, 540Nm torque (SLK 55 AMG, R172 launch)
2015 - M152.980 continues through end of R172 production

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz SLK 55 AMG Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The SLK 55 AMG's M113 and M152 V8s are among AMG's most celebrated naturally aspirated engines - hand-built masterpieces from Affalterbach. The M113 is widely regarded as one of the most reliable AMG engines ever produced, with a legendary reputation for durability [1†L6-L7]. The M152 is a two-generation leap forward, offering a better soundtrack and higher redline [7†L45-L46]. However, both have well-documented weaknesses that can lead to significant repair costs. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: M113 Oil Leaks & Crank Sensor Failure
problems.h4: M113 Oil Leaks & Crank Sensor Failure - The R171 SLK 55 AMG's Common Issues
problems.rootCause: The M113 V8 is known for oil leaks from valve cover gaskets and the rear main seal [9†L36-L37]. The crankshaft position sensor is a well-documented failure point, typically around 90,000 miles, causing hot-start failure - the car will start from cold fine but won't start when hot [12†L32-L33]. Oil pump pickup tube O-ring failure can cause low oil pressure, exacerbated by high oil temperatures and track use [1†L11-L14][12†L27-L29].

problems.recommendation: The M113's crank sensor is a known weak point - keeping a spare in the glove box is a common owner recommendation [12†L33-L35]. Oil leaks on the M113 are common with age but not usually urgent unless they are heavy. Valve cover gasket replacement at a specialist is significantly cheaper than dealer rates. If you experience hot-start failure, replace the crank sensor immediately - it's a cheap and straightforward fix that prevents being stranded.

problems.group: M152 Camshaft Follower & Rocker Arm Wear
problems.h4: M152 Camshaft Follower & Rocker Arm Wear - The R172 SLK 55 AMG's Valve Train Issue
problems.rootCause: The M152 can suffer from cam follower and rocker arm failure [7†L5-L6][2†L24-L27]. Symptoms include engine noise (tapping, ticking, or popping), rough running, lack of performance, and engine stalling [7†L5-L6][7†L11-L13]. Failure can be caused by stuck or sticking engine valves [7†L7-L8]. Carbon buildup on intake valves can also cause them to not seat properly, leading to air and fuel leakage during compression and combustion [7†L23-L25]. Replacing cam followers and rocker arms is recommended in sets to prevent future failures [2†L27-L29].

problems.group: M113/M152 Exhaust Flap & Engine Mount Issues
problems.h4: M113/M152 Exhaust Flap & Engine Mount Issues - The AMG V8's Age-Related Problems
problems.rootCause: The M152's twin-pipe exhaust system has adjustable flaps that affect exhaust noise - at engine speeds below 2,000 rpm, the flaps remain closed [2†L31-L34]. Exhaust flap issues are more common than engine problems on the M152 [2†L7]. Engine vibration at idle can be caused by low idle speed or hard engine mounts, affecting vehicles up to chassis number 171.473#F029282 [9†L5-L7]. Heavy engine use can cause engine mounts to wear out [9†L10].
